markdown_content: ## Pattern Drafter Overview in CLO 2025.2 This section explains the Pattern Drafter feature in CLO 2025.2, focusing on how it integrates with avatars in the 3D workspace to automate sewing, arranging, and draping patterns. It introduces the process of accessing the Pattern Drafter and selecting pattern types such as trousers and skirts. To use the Pattern Drafter effectively, ensure an avatar is present in the 3D workspace. This enables automatic sewing, arrangement, and draping of patterns onto the avatar upon simulation. Access the Pattern Drafter via the top menu: **2D > Pattern Drafter**. The interface initially presents a blank pattern canvas. Users can select the desired pattern type from options such as trousers or skirts. New updates include the addition of trousers and skirts as base pattern types. For example, selecting "trousers" allows further specification of fit types like "slacks," which then automatically appear in the 2D window for editing. --- ## Measurement Settings and Customization This section details how to customize measurements within the Pattern Drafter, including the difference between general, simple, and custom measurement modes, and how CLO handles missing data. Measurement options include: - **General**: A broad set of predefined measurements. - **Simple**: A reduced set of essential measurements for basic adjustments. - **Custom**: User-defined measurements with granular control. Using the settings tool, users can select which measurements to include or exclude. Unchecking measurements instructs CLO to infer and adjust related dimensions automatically, granting the software more liberty to fill gaps based on existing inputs. Conversely, checking more measurements offers tighter user control, preventing CLO from modifying unchecked values. When in **Simple** mode, fewer measurements are visible, enabling quick edits via arrows or mouse controls. Adjustments are visually represented by yellow dotted lines indicating which pattern areas are affected. For example, editing the waistline affects primarily the front, but can influence the back depending on settings. Users can toggle control over specific pattern parts, such as the back waistline, by enabling or disabling those measurements in the settings. The "Total" option aggregates front and back adjustments — turning off "Total" isolates adjustments to the selected side only. --- ## Pattern Adjustment and Editing Tools This section covers detailed editing techniques using the Pattern Drafter, including adjusting widths, lengths, darts, and using style line tools for refining fit and shape. Key editable parameters for trousers include: - Waistline (front and back) - Hip width - Crop drop length (front and back) - Outseam style (curved or straight) - Leg opening width Newly introduced darts for pants can be shown or hidden. Their properties such as distance from center back, total width, and length are adjustable. For pants without darts, simply hide the dart feature. Example workflow: 1. Select a base trouser pattern. 2. Adjust waistline and hip width to desired values (e.g., waistline 34 inches, hip width 42 inches). 3. Modify crop drop lengths for front and back. 4. Toggle dart visibility and edit its dimensions. 5. Use the style line tool to refine curves and scale pattern pieces. 6. Simulate on the avatar to preview fit and make further refinements. The style line tool allows users to scale and reposition pattern lines dynamically. Holding shift while selecting enables multiple selections for grouped adjustments. Simulations update in real-time for rapid iteration. --- ## AI Integration for Pattern Generation This section describes the AI-powered pattern generation feature accessed via the "wand" icon, including text prompt-based pattern creation and image-based input. The AI pattern drafter allows users to generate patterns using: - **Text prompts**: Input descriptive phrases such as "trouser slacks straight ankle low men's classic," which CLO uses to generate a corresponding pattern. - **Image input**: Users can upload sketches or any images (e.g., found online) to guide pattern generation. Generated patterns appear automatically in the 2D window and can be created or deleted as needed. This tool supports both trouser and skirt pattern creation. --- ## Skirt Pattern Drafting and Editing This section explains how to draft and customize skirts using the Pattern Drafter, including setting measurements and editing curve points. Example skirt parameters include: - Waistline (e.g., 12 inches) - Hip height (e.g., 10.5 inches) - Hip width (e.g., 18 inches) - Length from center front (e.g., 25 inches) - Side seam length (e.g., 28 inches) - Hem/sweep width (e.g., 25 inches) - Seam curvature (curved or straight) Users can toggle darts off for skirts without darts. After creating the base pattern, simulation allows previewing the fit on the avatar. If the initial pattern is unsatisfactory, users can use the **Edit Curve Point** tool to manually adjust individual points and curves for precision shaping. For example, converting curve points to corner points and deleting unwanted points refines the shape. Matching measurements between adjoining points ensures accuracy and clean seams. The pattern can be iteratively adjusted by dragging points and changing curve types until the desired fit and style are achieved. --- ## Workflow Summary and Best Practices This section summarizes best practices for using the Pattern Drafter and emphasizes its role as a starting point for pattern making. - Always have an avatar present in the 3D workspace for automatic sewing and draping. - Use measurement settings wisely: more checked measurements mean greater user control; fewer mean CLO fills in gaps automatically. - Start with simple or custom measurement modes depending on your familiarity and needs. - Utilize darts and style line tools for detailed shaping. - Generate base patterns quickly using AI text prompts or image uploads. - Edit and refine patterns manually with curve point tools for perfect fit and style. - Use simulation frequently to preview fit and make iterative adjustments. - The Pattern Drafter is ideal for users who may not know how to draft patterns from scratch but want a solid base pattern to modify or hand off to a professional. This flexible approach allows for rapid prototyping and customization, saving time while retaining creative control. --- ## Additional Notes - CLO 2025.2’s Pattern Drafter continues to expand with new pattern types and features. - The AI pattern drafter supports multiple garment types including trousers, skirts, and tops. - Users should be aware that initial patterns may not be perfect and require manual adjustments. - The tool is designed to assist both novices and experienced pattern makers in creating base patterns quickly and efficiently.
